concept_use.Pole and polar for Circle: The polar of P(p,q) with respect to each circle (T = 0) and the condition that the two polars coincide give q = 0 and p^2 - 5p + 4 = 0.
concept_use.Chord of contact for Circle: For the point (4,0) outside C1 the polar is the chord of contact x = 1, whose length 2 sqrt 3 is asked.

english: Let $C_{1}:x^{2}+y^{2}=4$ and $C_{2}:x^{2}+y^{2}-12x+26=0$. There are exactly two points $P$ in the plane such that the polar of $P$ with respect to $C_{1}$ coincides with the polar of $P$ with respect to $C_{2}$, and exactly one of them lies outside $C_{1}$. Then the length of the chord of contact of the tangents drawn from this point to $C_{1}$ is
hindi: माना कि $C_{1}:x^{2}+y^{2}=4$ तथा $C_{2}:x^{2}+y^{2}-12x+26=0$ हैं। समतल में ठीक दो बिन्दु $P$ ऐसे हैं कि $C_{1}$ के सापेक्ष $P$ की ध्रुवी, $C_{2}$ के सापेक्ष $P$ की ध्रुवी के संपाती है, तथा इनमें से ठीक एक बिन्दु $C_{1}$ के बाहर स्थित है। तब इस बिन्दु से $C_{1}$ पर खींची गई स्पर्श रेखाओं की स्पर्श जीवा की लम्बाई है
solution: Coincident lines: $\dfrac{p-6}{p}=\dfrac{q}{q}=\dfrac{-6p+26}{-4}$ (for $q\neq0$ the first ratio gives $-6=0$, impossible), so $q=0$ and $\dfrac{p-6}{p}=\dfrac{6p-26}{4}$
$(1,0)$ is inside $C_{1}$; $(4,0)$ is outside. Its polar (chord of contact) w.r.t. $C_{1}$: $4x=4$, i.e. $x=1$
solution_full: For $P(p,q)$ the polar with respect to $C_{1}$ is $px+qy=4$.
With respect to $C_{2}$ ($g=-6$, $c=26$) the polar is $px+qy-6(x+p)+26=0$, i.e. $(p-6)x+qy+(26-6p)=0$.
Two lines coincide when their coefficients are proportional: $\dfrac{p-6}{p}=\dfrac{q}{q}=\dfrac{26-6p}{-4}$.
If $q\neq0$, the middle ratio is $1$, so $p-6=p$, impossible. Hence $q=0$, and the polars are the vertical lines $x=\dfrac{4}{p}$ and $x=\dfrac{6p-26}{p-6}$.
So the two points are $(1,0)$ and $(4,0)$ (the limiting points of the two circles). $(1,0)$ lies inside $C_{1}$ ($1<4$), and $(4,0)$ lies outside ($16>4$).
For the external point $(4,0)$ the polar with respect to $C_{1}$ is its chord of contact: $4x=4$, i.e. $x=1$.
The chord $x=1$ of $x^{2}+y^{2}=4$ has half-length $\sqrt{4-1}=\sqrt{3}$, so its length is $2\sqrt{3}$.
originality_note: New: the points whose polars with respect to two given circles coincide (the limiting points, never named in the stem) are found from proportional coefficients, then the external one supplies a chord of contact (way 4, a hidden structure). Closest known: polar of a given point; pole of a given line. Different because: the point is defined by an equality of two polars, which forces it onto the line of centres and leads to a quadratic.
stem_review: Read as a student: every point, curve and parameter is introduced, the conditions are complete, there is one reading, the answer is unique and equals the Answer Plan, the options have one form and the Hindi mirrors the English. Checked that C2 is a real circle (r^2 = 10), that exactly two such points exist and exactly one is outside C1, so 'this point' is unambiguous. Answer 2 sqrt 3 at (B) as planned. No change.
key_step: Set the two polars proportional, see that q must be 0, and solve p^2 - 5p + 4 = 0; then the chord of contact of (4,0).
justification: The defining property (equal polars) is unfamiliar and must be decoded through proportional coefficients, then linked to a chord of contact: two ideas linked. Placed with 2021-P1-Q1 (L3) and below the radical-axis anchor 2023-P2-Q13 (L4).
